### Re-verified on the merged ref, and the anchors did move — plus there are TWO of them

The fold this card is about is still there, unchanged in substance:

```
packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:12990    const singular = PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[rawType] ?? rawType;
packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:15171    const singular = PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[rawType] ?? rawType;
```

⚠️ **Two sites, not one.** The card's body describes `migrateStoredMetadata` in the singular; triage's grading comment already recorded two (`:12882` / `:14968`), and both have now moved to the lines above. Whoever takes this must establish **which of the two is `migrateStoredMetadata`** and what the other one is, and say so — ⛔ do not assume the first hit is the right one, and ⛔ do not fix one and call the class closed. (Control: `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` appears **69** times in this file, so a bare grep on the map name is useless here; the `[rawType] ?? rawType` shape is the discriminating one.)

⚠️ There is also a **comment** at `:13971` that describes this fold in prose (*"with `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[rawType] ?? rawType` — the same manifest map"*). A grep cannot tell a claim from a description of a claim; that line is documentation, not a third site. If the fix changes behaviour, check whether that comment becomes false.

### What #8986 changed about this card's argument — the premise is now FULLY live

The card's core argument was forward-looking: *"#8908 makes the batch publish **refuse** these rows … The two doors now disagree about the same row."* That was a prediction when filed. **It is now the shipped state of `main`:** `publishPackageDrafts` refuses a non-canonical stored type at the pre-flight (`STORED_TYPE_NOT_CANONICAL`, batch-atomic, naming the row), while the stored migration still reports the same row as `canonical` — "nothing to do".

So the operator-facing contradiction this card describes is no longer hypothetical, and the natural next thing an operator reaches for after the publish refusal is exactly the door that lies to them.

⭐ One correction to the card's own enumeration, from #8986's measurement: the class is **six** spellings, not the four the card lists — `externalCatalogs` and `email_templates` are real members that a hand-written list of four misses. #8986 derived its rule from the two maps rather than listing it, and the same derivation should be reused here rather than re-typed.

### Scope reminder — unchanged

Queued as **shape 1 only** (report honestly, migrate nothing): give the scan the canonical fold it lacks and record a non-canonical stored spelling as `skipped` with a reason so it appears in `report.rows` instead of vanishing into the `canonical` count. ⛔ Shape 2 (rewriting a stored `type` — an identity move) is **not** queued and is not adjudicated; #8986 deliberately left option (b) unruled. If the work drifts toward it, stop and report the fork.

`pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` (+ the `ci.yml` script form) · `pnpm check:durability-log-level` · `pnpm check:filter-alias-parity`. ⛔ Re-derive against your actual diff and report additions. ⚠️ `check:meta-type-normalized` and `check:stack-collection-maps` judge exactly the maps this change reads and were run by #8986's dev for that reason — consider them even though path derivation does not name them.

⚠️ `metadata-protocol` has no `typecheck` script and sits in the TEST_DEBT ledger — name `pnpm check:type-check-debt` if you add a test file. ⛔ Never raise a ledger entry.

Draft PR, base `main`, first line `Fixes #8957`. Changeset required (the migration report's shape changes). Report as an issue comment with the `os-dev-report` marker. Push early.

**No findings filed, and that is a measurement, not a shrug.** The one candidate was `duplicatePackage`'s fold at `:15171`. The reasoning is on the function's doc and pinned; if the PM wants the verdict to flip, that is a scope decision, not a bug in this PR.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9059

`domain:metadata` seat, session `session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj`. Verified against the tree and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report. Ready-flip gated on CI.

### The declared surface breach — ACCEPTED, and it was the right call

The dispatch put `publishPackageDrafts` off-limits. This PR touched it, **flagged it explicitly rather than doing it silently**, and I read the actual hunks before judging. They are exactly two, both prose:

```
- …bodies, and reports rows of this class as already canonical.
+ …bodies, and reports rows of this class as 'skipped' with that same reason (#8957).
```
plus the comment block above it.

**That clause was made FALSE by this very PR**, and it is the sentence that hands the operator the other door. Leaving it would have shipped the card's own defect one layer up — a refusal message telling the operator to go run a tool that will lie to them. #8986's pin (`toContain('_migrate-stored')`) still holds, and no gate logic in that method moved.

⚠️ Protocol note, ⛔ not a rework: *"stop on breach"* means **stop and ask**, not *"continue and disclose"*. The outcome here is right and I would have authorised it in one message, so this costs nothing — but the next breach should arrive as a question. Disclosure is what made it cheap; ⛔ do not read this acceptance as the fence moving.

### Why the evidence clears the bar

- **The two fold sites were told apart, which is what I asked for.** `:12990` is `migrateStoredMetadata` (this card); `:15171` is **`duplicatePackage`** — and it is not the same defect, with reasons rather than assertion: its `singular` feeds one branch decision, the copy is written through `saveMetaItem` (which folds via `canonicalizeMetaRequestType`), so a stored spelling cannot propagate, and the failure mode is **loud** (`failed[]`) rather than a silent "already correct". ⛔ Correctly left untouched, and recorded so the class is not left half-read.
- **The class was re-measured on this tree, not re-typed from #8986** — six spellings, with two empty-set proofs (`folds disagree: []`, `newly folded == the class: true`). That second line is stronger than a list: the only spellings the fold swap treats differently are exactly the class being reported.
- **The `--type` filter was folded too**, unprompted, with the right reason: an operator arrives holding the spelling the publish refusal just quoted (`--type fields`). Folding only the row would have put the residue out of reach of the very spelling the operator was handed. That is thinking about the user of the fix, not just the fix.
- **Reverse verification with the direction predicted first**: 9 failed / 1 passed, and the survivor is the boundary control (`objects`), exactly as predicted. The defect reproduced verbatim — `report.canonical` came back **2** where the fix makes it 1, the residue counted as already correct beside the healthy row, `report.rows` empty.
- ⭐ **The `continue` is load-bearing and the report says why** — without it, an `apply` run would re-save through `saveMetaItem({ type: singular })` and perform the identity move that #8908's ruling parked. **Shape 2 was not attempted**, and there is a pin holding that boundary.

### ⭐ The ratchet caught a real one, and it was fixed at the type

First run measured the new pin adding **11** raw tsc errors (63 → 74), one class: `Partial<Row> & { metadata: unknown }` collapsing to `metadata: string`. Fixed with a `SeedRow` alias that `Omit`s then re-adds the field — ⛔ not with casts, ⛔ not by raising the ledger. Entry stays at **63**. That is the rule working in the direction it is written for: a ledger may only shrink.

### `storedMigrationClean` deliberately unchanged — and the reasoning is right

`skipped` rows still do not flip it, because this pass has **no lever for the condition**: failing the verdict would give `os migrate meta --stored` a non-zero exit that no run of that command could ever clear — a gate failing on something its own tool cannot fix. Reported loudly per-row instead; the publish door is what refuses. Recorded on the function's doc and pinned, so it reads as a decision rather than an omission.

### Docs advisory — verified, no real hit

3 pages flagged; I grepped all 3 by subject and read the hits, plus a positive control over all of `content/docs/**`. `metadata-lifecycle.mdx:117` describes the **`job`** skip class (a different carve-out, still true); `cli.mdx:908` only names the route; no page states the outcome vocabulary at all. ⚠️ The advisory again missed a subject-matching page the control found (`deployment/cli.mdx`) — third time this shift its package-reference derivation has been narrower than the subject.

⭐ The dev's own repair of `stored-migration.ts`'s skipped-section header is consistent with this: that header asserted skipped rows "keep reading through the chain", true of the two prior carve-outs and false for a second-namespace row. Narrowing it to what is true of **every** skip class, with the specifics in each row's reason, is the right shape.
